title: wciwf-1995-world
label: Jumping Joey Smith

won.source: The fed's own Card #1 script (24 November 1995): a 20-man battle royal closes with 'the winner of the match and FIRST WCIWF WORLD CHAMPION -- JUMPING JOEY SMITH.'

how: Outlasted 19 other men in the fed's opening 20-man battle royal, last eliminating Barry the Bonecrusher, to become the inaugural champion.
note: Still recognized as champion when the surviving record breaks off, 1 December 1995.

title: wciwf-1995-tv
label: The Great Oni

won.source: The fed's own Card #1 script (24 November 1995): 'The winner of the match and NEW WCIWF TV CHAMPION IS -- THE GREAT ONI (11:33),' defeating The Jet in the title tournament's final.

how: Won an eight-man tournament final against The Jet with a top-rope Savate From the Top, to become the inaugural champion.
note: Still recognized as champion when the surviving record breaks off, 1 December 1995.

title: wciwf-1995-world-tag
label: The British Battlers

won.source: The fed's own Card #1 script (24 November 1995): 'The winners of the battle royal and World Champs are -- THE BRITISH BATTLERS,' the last team standing in a seven-team elimination gauntlet.

how: The British Battlers (Jumping Jack Jones and The Brown Bomber) outlasted six other teams in a seven-team elimination gauntlet, Jumping Jack Jones backdropping PAIN's Xtra Tuff over the top for the final elimination, to become the inaugural champions.
note: Still recognized as champions when the surviving record breaks off, 1 December 1995.

title: wciwf-1995-us-tag
label: PAIN

won.source: The fed's own Card #1 script (24 November 1995): 'And the US Tag champs are -- PAIN,' the last team eliminated before the final two in the same seven-team gauntlet that decided the World Tag title above.

how: PAIN (Xtra Tuff and Everlasting Payne) were the last team eliminated before the final two in the fed's seven-team tag gauntlet, named US Tag champions under that battle royal's own dual-stakes stipulation.
note: Still recognized as champions when the surviving record breaks off, 1 December 1995.
